newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UK's Clarke says was proved right on rates.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says was proved right on rates.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Friday that events had proved him right in his public disagreement with Bank of England governor Eddie George over interest rates.
According to recently published notes of a December 11 monetary policy meeting with the governor, Clarke rejected George's call for a quarter point rate rise.
"Subsequent figures about what was going on (in the economy) reinforced my judgement," he told journalists at the World Economic Forum, referring to his decision to reject the governor's advice.
He said that he had decided against any move in interest rates after data showed that a rapid acceleration of the economy in November did not carry through into December.
The information about underlying cost pressures in the economy were also very good, he added.
Clarke said that he would continue to act in accordance with his target for an inflation rate of 2.5 percent but declined to comment further on the likely trend of rates.
He began the news conference by saying he would neither discuss exchange rates nor interest rates.
